title: Build a WaveNet and generate one sample at a time
brief: Implement mu-law coding, dilated causal convolutions, the gated residual stack, and cached generation that matches the parallel forward pass, then train a WaveNet on a sung vowel.
hints: mu_law_encode: np.log1p(mu * np.abs(x)) / np.log1p(mu) is the companded magnitude; put the sign back, then np.floor((f + 1) / 2 * mu + 0.5).astype(np.int64).
causal_conv1d: pad (K - 1) * dilation zeros on the left only with F.pad(x, (left, 0)), then call F.conv1d with the same dilation and no padding.
WaveNet.forward: the embedding gives (B, T, C); transpose it to (B, C, T) before the first convolution. Each layer adds its residual to x and its skip to a running sum.

WaveNet.step: the dilated kernel has two taps. weight[:, :, 1] multiplies the current input and weight[:, :, 0] the input d steps back, which is cache[i][:, :, 0]. A 1x1 convolution on one time step is a matrix product with weight[:, :, 0].
generate: keep the cache from each call and pass it to the next; build the Generator once, before the loop, so the seed fixes the whole sequence.
